diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, set $m_j = j(k/d_1)^{-1}p \bmod{N_1}$ for the row index

issues.failure_explanation: With d_1 = gcd(k, N_1), the quotient k/d_1 is coprime only to N_1/d_1 = D_1, not to N_1. Example: N_1 = 12, k = 8 gives d_1 = 4 and k/d_1 = 2, which has no inverse mod 12. So m_j and n_j are undefined in general, and the proof that every residue j is attained is unsupported as written.

failure_location.quote: $k/d_1$ and $l/d_2$ must have multiplicative inverses modulo $N_1$ and $N_2$, respectively

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take inverses of k/d_1 and l/d_2 modulo D_1 and D_2 only. Then m_j(k/d_1) ≡ jp (mod D_1) already gives m_j k ≡ jp d_1 (mod N_1), and the rest of the argument goes through unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of a solution (m_j, n_j) for each j rests on this step. It is used to show that every entry of X is defined in the construction of Lemma amb2D and to get the coset count M = N_1N_2/D. The statement is likely still true, but the proof is incomplete.
issues.title: False invertibility claim for k/d_1 modulo N_1 in the existence part of Lemma subsig
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local change of modulus and keeps the lemma, the method and all conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $D_1/p < D_1$, the $(pk,pl)$-subsignal was recovered at a previous iteration of the for loop in Line~\ref{ln:outer}.

issues.failure_explanation: The identity gcd(pk, N_1) = p·gcd(k, N_1) holds only when p divides D_1 = N_1/gcd(k, N_1). Example: N_1 = 6, k = 3, p = 3 gives gcd(9 mod 6, 6) = 3, but p·gcd(k, N_1) = 9. When k = 0 and D_1 = 1, D_1/p is not an integer. In these cases p divides N_1 but not D_1, so D_1 does not decrease and the case split does not show that the (pk, pl)-subsignal comes earlier in the loop order. The needed split is p | D_1 versus p ∤ D_1, with D_2 decreasing in the second case.

failure_location.quote: If $p \divs N_1$, then $\gcd(pk, N_1) = p\gcd(k, N_1) = N_1/(D_1/p)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split on whether p divides D_1 or D_2. If p | D_1, then D_1 drops to D_1/p. If p ∤ D_1, then D_1 is unchanged and p | D_2, so D_2 drops to D_2/p, which is an earlier inner iteration. This also requires increasing-order iteration over divisors, which the algorithm states only in prose.
issues.overall_effect: The stated justification that all decimated subsignals needed by the ILP are available when Algorithm memo_2D reaches (k, l) is incorrect as written. The ordering itself appears to still work.
issues.title: Incorrect gcd identity in the iteration-order verification for Memoized 2D Inversion
issues.why_classification: A short corrected case analysis restores the correctness argument with no change to the algorithm.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The $60 \times 60$ matrix required $350 / 3600 \approx 9.7\%$ of DFT coefficients

issues.failure_explanation: The 60x60 figure uses the table's coefficient count (350, with conjugates). For 11x13 at M = 5 the same table lists 16 coefficients, which is 16/143 ≈ 11.2%, not 8/143. Counted consistently, the 11x13 case needs a larger fraction than the 60x60 case (11.2% versus 9.7%). This contradicts the claim that 11x13 was inverted 'from a relatively smaller sampled spectrum'.

failure_location.quote: whereas the $11 \times 13$ matrix required $8 / 143 \approx 5.6\%$ of DFT coefficients for reliable inversion

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use one counting convention for both cases (16/143 ≈ 11.2% versus 350/3600 ≈ 9.7%) and revise the conclusion to say the two cases are comparable, with 11x13 slightly higher.
issues.overall_effect: The conclusion drawn from this comparison is unsupported by the paper's own table. The related remark that the two cases are 'comparable' needs restating.
issues.title: Inconsistent coefficient count in the 11x13 versus 60x60 sampling-fraction comparison
issues.why_classification: It is a local numerical and interpretive correction that does not affect any theorem, algorithm or the main experimental conclusions.
